_comment: The map-shaped half of tools/live-gate: everything the sixteen steps need
to know about THIS map, so the driver holds the checks and this holds the
coordinates. A second map is a second file, not a second driver.
Every number here was read off a live dm_lockdown with ./debug-api and is
reproducible: `debug-api mapents dm_lockdown` for the brush entities,
`debug-api ents "*"` for the census, `debug-api aim` for the sight lines.
_census: 485 / 63 since 2026-10-27, read off a live dm_lockdown with a client joined
(`debug-api ents "*"`, debug, lane t6-globals). From 473 / 61: +17 for
func_useableladder (3) and info_ladder_dismount (14), managed entities since
0dffef1db; -5 spotlight_end, since an unnamed point_spotlight removes its end
as stock's Activate does (435e890d1; stock leaves 4).
_otherMap: THE MAP-CHANGE STEP'S TARGET. Not a second deathmatch map -- there is only
one of those on this box -- but ss_sandbox, which `make map MAP=ss_sandbox`
builds from Sandbox.cs and whose own gate asserts that EVERY class the mod
registers has an instance in it and that every temp entity it sends has a
station that fires it. Changing to it and back is therefore a teardown of
one of everything, which is exactly what a level-shutdown defect needs.
THE FLOORS ARE FLOORS AND THE EQUALITY IS THE ASSERTION. minEntities and
minClasses only have to be un-clearable by an empty or half-loaded level;
what pins the number is the step's own cross-pass comparison, which
requires the SECOND visit in one process to read exactly what the first
did. A count that drifts between two visits is a leak.
mustHold is there because a census is a number and a map is what is in it:
a game that answered about the map it never left would clear both floors.
ss_te_tester is the classname Sandbox.cs places 43 of, one per temp entity
the mod sends, and dm_lockdown holds none.
_otherMapMeasured: READ OFF A LIVE ss_sandbox on 2026-09-14, both passes of one process:
1234 entities / 271 classes, and 43 ss_te_tester. The floors below are set
under those at roughly 90% -- tight enough that a half-loaded level or a
game answering about the map it never left cannot clear them (dm_lockdown
is 485 / 63), loose enough that regenerating the map from Sandbox.cs with
one class more or less does not turn the gate red for a reason that is not
a defect. What pins the number exactly is the step's own cross-pass
equality, which needs no constant here at all.

_switchedPairs: Classes whose count is a lamp's STATE: a lit point_spotlight owns one
spotlight_end and one ss_beam. The weighed plate's drum lights one about
0.6s after level start and, in 9 of 40 visits (reload-probe, f48aeb1),
leaves the plate and douses it at ~8s. The cross-visit equality forgives the two
moving together and nothing else (census_drift in tools/live-gate).
_renderPoses: render-plan-sandbox compares at the spawn the client joins at and at these: under the
mirror pool's surface (the under-water fixture's pose). ss_sandbox's view lists hold
renderables that are not entities, which dm_lockdown's do not: the draw batch's

_openFloor: Flat, walled-off floor in the yard south of the showers. The player is put
here for every step that needs room: it is far from the map's scripted
triggers (which explode walls), it has 300+ units of clear sight along +Y,
and looking 25 degrees down puts the aim point on the floor about 105
units ahead -- which is where ent_create and prop_physics_create put what
_pushFloor: Where the push step walks into its crate: openFloor moved 323 units east,
same angles. openFloor's own path to the crate crosses eight concrete_chunk
props the map lays on the floor (-3980..-3804, 2952..3036); a player who
steps onto one stands on physics, which turns the push's lean off (stock,
player.cpp:4811), and the pair creeps at 1-12 u/s. tools/pushprobe,
physics-managed 2a89728f: 6-13 jams per run there; here 1 of 20 holds, with
player and crate walking at 48-52 u/s, stock's push cap (player.cpp:8233).
The knock-loose step walks the same line to its pinned crate: at openFloor
18 of 20 knock holds jammed, here 0 of 20, every crate knocked loose.
_trigger: trigger_multiple *20, whose ONLY connection is OnStartTouch -> PlaySound.
Chosen for being inert: dm_lockdown's other triggers Explode walls and Kill
brushes, and a gate that rearranges the map it is measuring cannot then
wind: fan_wind, the trigger_push over the same floor (speed 800, toward the
fan), which the fan's angular-velocity sensor enables once the fan spins up.
It blows a player in the room about, as stock's does, which the step's
shadow catch-ups cannot measure; the step turns it off and back on after.
_door: showers_gate3 slides 130 units along +Y on Open (movedir 0 90 0, wait -1 so
it stays open). tport_switch_cover_1 is the rotating kind and turns to yaw
160. Both are checked, because 'a door opened' is two different mechanisms.
_lift: dm_lockdown HAS NO LIFT -- no func_plat, no func_tracktrain, no vertical
func_door; its three doors all move horizontally and its brush models are
4-unit-thin plates nobody could ride. So the gate BUILDS one: a
func_movelinear wearing brush model *7 (a 64x112x2 plate, flat side up)
pointed straight up. movedir is a QAngle, not a vector -- '0 0 1' reads as
yaw 0 and moves the lift sideways, which is how this was first written and
how it first passed while measuring nothing.
The lift is Killed at the end of its step so the next census is the map's.
_pickups: item_healthkit gives 25 and only takes if the player is hurt, so the damage
step runs first. Ammo is trickier: a weapon's Reserve only shows the pool
of the ACTIVE weapon's ammo type, so the gate gives an smg1 (which arrives
with a full clip and an EMPTY reserve), makes it active, and then walks
onto an item_ammo_smg1. Reserve 0 -> non-zero is the pickup.
_projectile: NOT one of the sixteen, and here because `shoot` IS HITSCAN. The SMG's
shot is a trace applied the same tick and nothing is ever in the air, so a
build whose flight integrator (plan_entity.md step 2f, EntityMotion.cs)
was never registered passes `shoot` unchanged. Step 2f measured that,
said so in its handover, and left the gate to whoever owns it.
FIRED FLAT, pitch 0, along openFloorAngles' yaw. The yard's far wall is
367 units away at eye height and that is what step 2f's separate probe
recorded for both ss_bolt and ss_rocket standing here. At the scenario's
own 25-degrees-down angle a bolt is in the floor after 123.9 units, which
is why this step sets its own pitch instead of reusing openFloorAngles.
minTravel 200 SITS BETWEEN TWO MEASURED NUMBERS and --self-test asserts
it lies strictly between them, because a threshold outside that interval
makes the step a check that cannot fail in one direction or cannot pass
in the other:
stationary 68.4 -- where a bolt sits when the integrator is not run.
IT IS NOT ZERO, and that is the whole reason this number is written
down: a shot leaves from the EYE, 64 units above the player's origin,
so a projectile that never moves an inch is still 68.4 units from the
shooter. A travel threshold under 68.4 would pass on a build that
flies nothing. Measured by disabling EntityMotion.RunFrame, not
reasoned about: every sighting of the unmoved bolt read 68.4.
recordedTravel 367.0 -- what a bolt that DOES fly reaches here, on this
branch and in step 2f's independent probe.
minTargetRange 150 is the floor under the crate arm: `ent_create` puts the
crate where the player LOOKS and it then falls and slides, so where it
ends up is measured each run rather than assumed. Observed 269.7 and
338.3 in two probe runs. The range is CHECKED, not noted -- a crate that
landed at the player's feet would still be destroyed and would prove
nothing about travel.
AND ONE DRAW OF THAT CRATE IS A COIN FLIP, which those two probe runs
were too few to show. Lane 3f later read 111.5 -- UNDER the 150 floor --
and the gate went red on a step whose subject (does a bolt fly and hit)
was never reached. Three readings of the SAME commit disagreed about
`projectile` for this reason and nothing else. The step now resamples the
target up to PROJECTILE_TARGET_TRIES times and keeps the furthest draw;
the floor is unchanged, because the floor is not what was wrong. 111.5 is
only 43 units above the 68.4 an unflown bolt reads, so lowering it to fit
that draw would have taken the meaning out of the assertion.
AND THE COIN FLIP WAS A BUG, not a fixture that needed more draws. Lane
diag-gateseq measured it: `ent_create` set the crate's ORIGIN to the aim
point, and wood_crate001a's origin is 28 units above its base, so every
crate was born 28 units inside the floor and vphysics threw it 29 to 164
units clear. THAT ejection was the extra distance -- 269.7 and 338.3 are
readings of it. With `shoot`'s gibs at the aim point the ejection went
sideways or backwards (bearing 180 against a clean draw's 82), and in one
round of three it came out the WRONG SIDE and the crate rested at
z = -5935, which is lane 3f-shadow's prop-fall.
targetPitch 11 is the repair, and it is a fixture built by GEOMETRY rather
than by an ejection. openFloorAngles' 25 degrees puts the aim point 140
units out from a 64-unit eye, which is under minTargetRange and always
was; 11 degrees puts it 324.1 units out on flat floor (z 1.02) and the
crate settles at 322.8, identically on every draw of every round.
--self-test asserts 64/tan(targetPitch) clears minTargetRange with margin
and that it is SHALLOWER than openFloorAngles, so the constant is
checkable without a live game. minTargetRange itself is untouched: the
fixture was what was wrong, and it still is not the threshold.
_effects: rope-settle and beam-ring (plan_client_novalve 5.3): both read the managed
effect counters through their console readouts (cs_cl_rope_spans,
cs_cl_beams) and flip the managed draw switch (r_drawropes, r_DrawBeams) for
the flat side of the A/B. The poses are the C2 lane's recording poses
in view from ropePose, and a ring fired at beamRing is in view, in the PVS
and inside the frustum from beamPose.
_renderPoses: The render plan's other recorded poses (src/test/client/Fixtures/render-stock/README.md):
render-plan compares stock and plan at each as well as at the stand, so the live evidence
covers every pose the oracle holds (C7 step 2).
